paper.title: Group-Fair Online Allocation in Continuous Time

settings.name_in_paper: Continuous-time online learning for group-fair utility maximization under time budget B (delayed full-information feedback)
unmapped: Each decision is a (group, deadline) pair from [K] x a finite deadline set of size L; task occupies random completion time min{X, t} of a continuous time budget B
Objective is sum of concave utilities U_k of per-group reward rates (alpha-fair utilities), not total reward
Reward collected only if random completion time is below chosen deadline; completion time and reward may be correlated
settings.definition_quote: the total utility under a policy $\pi$ is defined as: $$U^\pi(B) = \sum_{k=1}^KU_k\big(\overline{r}^\pi_k(B)\big)$$ ... {\tt REG}_\Pi^\pi(B)={\tt OPT}_\Pi(B)-U^\pi(B) ... We assume a delayed full-information feedback model where the completion time and reward of all groups for task $n$ are revealed to the controller at stage $n+\tau$ for some delay $\tau \geq 1$.

conditions: utility functions U_k continuously differentiable, concave, increasing
finite deadline set; completion times positive; rewards bounded
regret measured against best stationary randomized policy class Pi_S

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: For any $V>0$ and constant delay $\tau$, the regret under $\pi^{\tt OLUM}$ is bounded as ${\tt REG}_{\Pi_S}{^{\pi^{\tt OLUM}}}(B) = O\Big(\sqrt{\frac{\log(B)}{B}} + \frac{V}{B}+\frac{1}{V}\Big).$

results.notes: Regret is the difference in utility of reward rates (per unit time), not cumulative reward; kept as stated (not multiplied by B) since utilities are nonlinear. Quantity set to 'other'. Delay tau mapped to D.

conditions: utility functions U_k continuously differentiable, concave, increasing
regret measured against best stationary randomized policy class Pi_S

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: By choosing $V = \Theta(\sqrt{B/\log(B)})$, we obtain ${\tt REG}_{\Pi_S}{^{\pi^{\tt OLUM}}}(B) = O(\sqrt{\log(B)/B})=\tilde{O}(1/\sqrt{B})$.

results.notes: Tuned version; requires knowing B. Regret is in utility-of-rate units (vanishing with B).
